title: Normal projective compactification with constant geometric boundary primes
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], and let $X$ be a smooth geometrically integral affine finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible, def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. There exist a finite-type $k$-scheme $C$, a closed immersion $C\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_k$ for some finite $n$ [def-kun-projective], and a dense open immersion $j:X\hookrightarrow C$ [def-weil-open-immersion] such that $C$ is geometrically integral and geometrically normal. Geometrically normal means that for every field extension $F/k$ [def-pc-field-extension] all local rings of $C_F=C\times_k\operatorname{Spec}F$ are integrally closed domains. In particular every $C_F$ is integral, normal, Noetherian (covered by finitely many spectra of Noetherian rings) and proper over $F$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Write $B_1,\ldots,B_r$ for the reduced irreducible components of $C\setminus j(X)$ of codimension one; $r$ is finite and may be zero. Here codimension one means that the local ring at the generic point has Krull dimension one. Each $B_i$ is geometrically integral. For every extension $F/k$, the reduced subschemes $(B_i)_F$ are precisely, without repetition, the codimension-one irreducible components of $C_F\setminus j_F(X_F)$. The fibre products use [def-pc-fibre-product], and geometric integrality has its every-field-extension meaning [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible].

source.place: Agent-assembled geometric compactification interface: normalization of projective closure, Tag 0GK4 (lemma-normalize-projective); Tag 038N (lemma-geometrically-normal-at-point); Tags 020I (lemma-perfect-reduced), 020J (lemma-separably-closed-irreducible). The projective closure is morphisms.tex Tag 01WA (lemma-H-quasi-projective-open-H-projective); preservation of boundary dimensions uses algebra.tex Tag 00P3 (lemma-dimension-preserved-field-extension).

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-compactification-affine] to obtain a dense open immersion $X\hookrightarrow P$ with $P$ projective. Replace $P$ by its reduction $P_0$, using [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction]. This is a closed subscheme with the same underlying space. Its restriction to the open $X$ is $X$ itself, because $X$ is integral and therefore reduced: on an affine chart the nilradical restricts to zero on this open. Thus $X\hookrightarrow P_0$ is still a dense open immersion. The space $P_0$ is irreducible, since it contains the dense irreducible subspace $X$; being reduced and nonempty it is integral. Composing its closed immersion into $P$ with $P\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^n_k$ is a closed immersion (on local rings, compose the quotient maps), so $P_0$ is projective by [def-kun-projective]. The space $\mathbf P^n_k$ is covered by its $n+1$ standard affine charts, so it is quasi-compact, and its closed subset $P_0$ is quasi-compact; hence $P_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is also projective in the quasi-compact convention of [def-pc-projective-morphism]. By [lem-pc-projective-proper] it is proper, hence finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: Tag 0GK4 (lemma-normalize-projective), with morphisms.tex Tag 01WA (lemma-H-quasi-projective-open-H-projective); reduction of the dense projective closure.

proof.text:
Let $
u:C=P_0^
u	o P_0$ be normalization in its own function field [def-sc-normalization]. The projective-normalization theorem [lem-weil-pbc-normalization-projective-components] gives a normal integral projective proper $C$: here $P_0$ has exactly one reduced irreducible component, so the componentwise normalization in that theorem has one summand and is exactly $P_0^
u$. In particular $C$ is finite type. The base $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is normal, since its only local ring is the field $k$, an integrally closed domain. Applying [lem-sfb-smooth-normal-ascent] to $X	o\operatorname{Spec}k$ shows that $X$ is normal. Consequently [lem-sc-normalization-over-normal-locus] identifies $
u^{-1}(X)	o X$ with an isomorphism. Its inverse followed by the open inclusion defines $j:X\hookrightarrow C$. It has nonempty image, and this image is dense because $C$ is integral. Projectivity supplies the required finite projective-space embedding.

The field $k$ is perfect: in positive characteristic $p$, a root in $k$ of $T^p-a$ is a $p$th root of each $a\in k$; characteristic zero already satisfies the definition of perfect. It is also separably closed, since every nonconstant polynomial has a root, so every irreducible polynomial has degree one. In [lem-weil-pbc-normality-perfect-closure-test] take $K=k$; the power condition holds with exponent index zero. Normality of $C$ therefore implies normality of every $C_F$, for arbitrary $F/k$. Taking $\Omega=k$ and $A=|C|$ in [lem-sbc-subset-geometric-irreducibility] proves that every $C_F$ is nonempty and irreducible. A scheme with domain local rings is reduced, so these schemes are integral. This proves geometric normality and geometric integrality with precisely the every-field-extension meanings in the statement.

source.place: Tags 038O (lemma-geometrically-normal) and 020J (lemma-separably-closed-irreducible), specializing the perfect-closure test to the perfect field itself.

proof.text: By step 2, $C$ is proper, hence of finite type and in particular quasi-compact over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism]; with its closed immersion into $\mathbf P^n_k$, $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is projective in the convention of [def-pc-projective-morphism]. For every $F/k$, projectivity of $C_F\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ in that convention follows from [lem-pc-projective-base-change]. Thus [lem-pc-projective-proper] and [def-weil-proper-morphism] make $C_F$ proper and finite type. A field is Noetherian (its only ideals are zero and the whole field), so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] shows that $C_F$ is Noetherian, including the finite affine-cover assertion in the statement. This also applies to $F=k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], $j_F$ is an open immersion. Write $Z=|C|\setminus j(X)$ and let $p:C_F\to C$ be projection. The complement of $j_F(X_F)$ is $p^{-1}Z$: the pullback of an open subscheme is its inverse-image open, as is seen directly by restricting the fibre-product universal property.

source.place: Tag 0GK4 (lemma-normalize-projective), projective permanence; morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); base change of the open complement.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components], the closed subset $Z$ has finitely many distinct irreducible components $T_1,\ldots,T_s$; when $Z$ is empty use $s=0$. Give $T_a$ its reduced induced closed subscheme structure $D_a\hookrightarrow C$ by [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Each $D_a$ is reduced, nonempty and irreducible, hence integral. It is finite type over $k$: on each affine chart of the finite-type scheme $C$ its ring is a quotient of the chart ring, still a finitely generated $k$-algebra, and a finite affine cover of $C$ restricts to a finite affine cover of $D_a$. This verifies the finite-type hypothesis required for each use of geometric reducedness and dimension below.

source.place: properties.tex Tag 0BA8 (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components); schemes.tex reduced induced closed subscheme construction; preparation for Tags 020I and 020J.

proof.text: Fix any $F/k$. Apply [lem-sbc-subset-geometric-irreducibility] with $\Omega=k$, $X=D_a$, and its whole underlying set to show that $(D_a)_F$ is nonempty and irreducible. Since $k$ is perfect and $D_a$ is reduced of finite type, [lem-kun-geometric-reduced-perfect] says $(D_a)_F$ is reduced. Thus every $D_a$ is geometrically integral. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $(D_a)_F\hookrightarrow C_F$ is a closed immersion; its image is $p^{-1}T_a$. Indeed, locally it is $\operatorname{Spec}((R/I)\otimes_kF)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_kF)$, whose image is the zero set of the extended ideal $I$. The projection $(D_a)_F\to D_a$ is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change], applied to the surjective map $\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. Finite type of $(D_a)_F$ follows from [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change].

source.place: Tags 020I (lemma-perfect-reduced) and 020J (lemma-separably-closed-irreducible); affine quotient description of base change of closed immersions.

proof.text: The subsets $p^{-1}T_a$ cover $p^{-1}Z$, and are irreducible closed by step 6. They have no containment relations: a containment $p^{-1}T_a\subseteq p^{-1}T_b$ would imply $T_a\subseteq T_b$ by surjectivity of $(D_a)_F\to D_a$, hence $a=b$. An irreducible subset of a finite union of closed subsets lies in one of them (otherwise its intersections with these closed subsets give a finite proper closed covering, contradicting irreducibility). Therefore the $p^{-1}T_a$ are exactly, without repetitions, all irreducible components of $p^{-1}Z$. Their reduced induced structures are $(D_a)_F$, by uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme], since these are already reduced closed subschemes with those supports.

source.place: Tags 020I and 020J followed by the finite-union irreducibility argument; uniqueness of the reduced induced closed subscheme.

proof.text:
By [lem-sc-scheme-sober], let $\eta_a$ be the unique generic point of $D_a$, viewed also as a point of $C$. Its local ring on $D_a$ is its function field [def-sc-function-field], so has dimension zero. The formula [lem-kun-dimension-formula] for $D_a$ and [lem-sc-dimension-locally-algebraic] give $\dim D_a=\operatorname{trdeg}_k\kappa(\eta_a)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-residue-field-iso] this residue field is the same on $C$. Apply the same dimension formula and local constancy of dimension to the integral scheme $C$ to obtain
$\dim C=\dim\mathcal O_{C,\eta_a}+\dim D_a$.
The same argument over $F$ gives
$\dim C_F=\dim\mathcal O_{C_F,\eta_{a,F}}+\dim(D_a)_F$.
By [lem-kun-dimension-extension], $\dim C_F=\dim C$ and $\dim(D_a)_F=\dim D_a$. All these dimensions are finite for the present nonempty finite-type schemes, by [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], so cancellation proves equality of the two displayed local-ring dimensions. In particular a component has codimension one exactly when its base-changed component does. Enumerate those $D_a$ with codimension one as $B_1,\ldots,B_r$. Steps 6--7 give geometric integrality and the asserted precise boundary list over every $F/k$. If none has codimension one, $r=0$ and the same argument gives the empty list after extension.

Step 6: the image of the base-changed boundary is p^{-1}T_a, checked by contracting primes of R⊗F.
